name: 46,XY Difference of Sexual Development Due to Dihydrotestosterone Backdoor Pathway Biosynthesis Defect
aliases: 46,XY DSD due to DHT Backdoor Pathway Defect
46,XY Disorder of Sexual Development from Dihydrotestosterone Biosynthesis Abnormality

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Biochemical Diagnostic Criteria for 46,XY DSD due to DHT Backdoor Pathway Defect

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in the dihydrotestosterone backdoor pathway (e.g., AKR1C2, AKR1C4)
Abnormal steroid profile showing reduced dihydrotestosterone levels with elevated alternative androgen precursors consistent with backdoor pathway disruption
Presence of undervirilized external genitalia in a 46,XY individual including micropenis, hypospadias, or ambiguous genitalia
Absence or hypoplasia of male internal genital structures on pelvic ultrasound or MRI
Family history of similar phenotypes or known genetic mutations affecting androgen biosynthesis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical phenotype consistent with undervirilization in 46,XY individual plus confirmatory biochemical profile and genetic testing identifying pathogenic variants in backdoor pathway genes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including endocrinology, genetics, and radiology.

pathognomonic.notes: Significantly reduced penile length relative to age and gestational norms
Abnormal urethral meatus location on ventral penile shaft
Genitalia not clearly male or female in appearance

common.notes: Shortened distance between anus and genitalia
searchTerms: short distance between anus and genitals

common.symptomName: Delayed or absent virilization during puberty
common.notes: Lack of expected secondary sexual characteristics
Breast tissue development in affected individuals

occasional.notes: Dysuria or spraying of urine stream
searchTerms: difficulty urinating due to mild hypospadias

occasional.symptomName: Psychosocial distress related to genital ambiguity
occasional.notes: Emotional or psychological impact due to atypical genitalia
searchTerms: psychosocial issues due to unclear genitalia
mental health impact of ambiguous genitals

rare.notes: Rare development of germ cell tumors in dysgenetic gonads
Rare cases with adrenal steroidogenesis disruption
searchTerms: high blood pressure from adrenal gland problems

imaging: Pelvic ultrasound or MRI showing absent or hypoplastic male internal genitalia (e.g., seminal vesicles, vas deferens abnormalities)
Undescended testes visualized in inguinal canal or abdomen
genetic: Pathogenic variants in AKR1C2, AKR1C4, or other genes involved in the DHT backdoor biosynthesis pathway
other: Histopathology of gonadal tissue may show dysgenetic features
Endocrine stimulation tests showing impaired DHT response

distinguishingFeatures: Normal or elevated androgen levels with end-organ resistance
Reduced conversion of testosterone to DHT due to SRD5A2 mutations
Similar undervirilization but with different steroid profile
Often virilization at puberty due to increased testosterone

redFlags: Ambiguous genitalia in a 46,XY neonate requiring urgent endocrine and genetic evaluation
Undescended testes with risk of malignancy
Delayed or absent puberty with lack of secondary sexual characteristics
references: Miller WL. Disorders in the initial steps of steroid hormone synthesis. J Steroid Biochem Mol Biol. 2017.
Hughes IA, et al. Consensus statement on management of intersex disorders. Arch Dis Child. 2006.
Orphanet: 46,XY difference of sexual development due to dihydrotestosterone backdoor pathway biosynthesis defect. ORPHA:443090.
